claim: The informativeness grade is sensitive to the rule that decides what counts as producer identity, and both readings are published as a declared sensitivity rather than one being discarded.
value: permissive reading, any token that is neither a published sentinel nor a generic word: 33,671 of 35,107 objects informative, 95.91 percent. Rule-table reading, only a value the published ordered rule table classifies as a named analysis: 4,799 of 35,107, 13.67 percent. The rule-table reading is the one reported.
floor: not applicable, no validator is involved: this is an attribute-content measurement read from the object
dropped: the permissive reading counted a viewer string, an acquisition vendor, an encoder sentinel and a device serial as producer identity; the values that decided it are named in results/ai_use.md
sop_class: seven complete census classes plus Segmentation Storage from the PRE-06 sample
status_note: The permissive rule is superseded and its code is not retained, so this row records the figure rather than a command that reproduces it. It is kept because the two readings differ by a factor of seven on the same objects, which is the largest single sensitivity in this paper and would be invisible if only the reported figure were published. The rule-table reading is reproducible and its residual, every value no rule matches, is published verbatim.
notes: Reported in Methods as a declared sensitivity, never as a range.
